subject: how scaled chi square difference is computed

messages.author: 71428bdc791d5c21
messages.subject: how scaled chi square difference is computed
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to understand how scaled chi square difference test in DWLS models is computed.

For example, if I test the measurement invariance between fit.configural and fit.loadings. The parameters are:
c1 = 1.459
c0 = 1.852
d1 = 734
d0 = 758
T1-DWLS= 1448.002 (robust = 1466.741)
T0-DWLS = 1601.482 (robust = 1360.415)

Lavaan gives me :

df-diff = 24
Chisq-diff = 11.0763
P(Chisq) = 0.9885


But if I try to compute myself Chisq-diff by using Satorra-Bentler method where:

cd = (d0 * c0 - d1*c1)/(d0 - d1)

df-diff = d0 - d1

Chisq-diff = (T0* c0 - T1*c1)/cd

Results are very different:

df-diff = 24
Chisq-diff = 61.52
P(Chisq) <=.001

The difference between Chi-squares is different but, essentially, the conclusions are totally opposite. If I use robust Chi-squares for computation, the difference is other but always p <=.001.

Does somebody know how lavaan computes the Chi-squares difference? Is it necessary to adjust the two Chi-squares before computation of the difference? If yes, how do that?

Thanks a lot for your help and best regards

Hclaude

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: how scaled chi square difference is computed
parts: I am trying to understand how scaled chi square difference test in DWLS models is computed.

It looks like you are referring to the method for scaling the chi-squared difference statistic using the Satorra-Bentler method, which is only a M adjustment.  When you use DWLS, you will get a MV adjustment (scaled and shifted statistic), so the formula applied here is not correct.

https://www.statmodel.com/chidiff.shtml

The correct method is described here, and compares Mplus to lavaan:

https://crmda.dept.ku.edu/guides/44.difftest/44.difftest.html
